body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Noble Deity <s>Mārīcī</s>!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma / jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhatrayodaśabhikṣuśataiḥ saṃbahulaiś ca mahāśrāvakabodhisatvamahāsatvaiḥ / tatra khalu bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma / asti bhikṣavo mārīcī nāma devatā sā sūryacandramāsoḥ purato 'nūpagacchati / sā na dṛśyate na gṛhyate na badhyate na nirudhyate na virudhyate na muṣyate na muhyate na daṇḍyate na muṇḍyate na dahyate na śatror anūpagacchati / yo 'pi tasya bhikṣavo mārīcīnāmadevatāyā nāma jānāti so 'pi na dṛśyate na gṛhyate na badhyate na nirudhyate na virudhyate na muṣyate na muhyate na daṇḍyate na muṇḍyate na dahyate na śatror anūpagacchati / so 'haṃ bhikṣavo mārīcīnāmadevatāyā nāma jānāmi / aham api @ayam api@@ na dṛśyate na badhyate na nirudhyate na virudhyate na muhyate na daṇḍyate na muṇḍyate na dahyate na śatror anūpagacchati / imāni mantrapadāni bhavanti / tadyathā ḥ oṃ padākramasi parākramasi udayamasi nairamasi arkamasi markamasi urmasi vanamasi gulmamasi cīvaramasi mahācīvaramasi antardhānamasi svāhā /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks)—thirteen hundred <s>bhikṣus</s>—and with many great <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> (great bodhisattva beings). Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: "There is, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, a deity named <s>Mārīcī</s> who walks before the sun and moon. She cannot be seen, cannot be seized, cannot be bound, cannot be obstructed, cannot be opposed, cannot be robbed, cannot be deluded, cannot be punished, cannot be shaved, cannot be burned, and she does not fall into the power of enemies. Whoever, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, knows the name of the deity <s>Mārīcī</s>, that person also cannot be seen, cannot be seized, cannot be bound, cannot be obstructed, cannot be opposed, cannot be robbed, cannot be deluded, cannot be punished, cannot be shaved, cannot be burned, and does not fall into the power of enemies. I, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, know the name of the deity <s>Mārīcī</s>. I too—and this one too—cannot be seen, cannot be bound, cannot be obstructed, cannot be opposed, cannot be deluded, cannot be punished, cannot be shaved, cannot be burned, and does not fall into the power of enemies." These are the <s>mantra</s> words: <s>tadyathā</s>: oṃ padākramasi parākramasi udayamasi nairamasi arkamasi markamasi ūrmasi vanamasi gulmamasi cīvaramasi mahācīvaramasi antardhānamasi <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: oṃ mārīcīdevatā pathe māṃ gopaya / utpathe māṃ gopaya / puruṣabhayato māṃ gopaya / rājabhayato māṃ gopaya / hastibhayato māṃ gopaya / caurabhayato māṃ gopaya / nāgabhayato māṃ gopaya / siṃhabhayato māṃ gopaya / vyāghrabhayato māṃ gopaya / aśvabhayato māṃ gopaya / (

children.text: ) agnibhayato māṃ gopaya / udakabhayato māṃ gopaya / sarpabhayato māṃ gopaya / viṣabhayato māṃ gopaya / sarvapratyarthikapratyamitrabhayato māṃ gopaya / ākuleṣu māṃ gopaya / anākuleṣu māṃ gopaya / mūrcchiteṣu māṃ gopaya / amūrcchiteṣu māṃ gopaya / nāgato me rakṣa / caṇḍamṛgato me rakṣa / rakṣa 2 mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvaduṣṭapraduṣṭebhyaḥ / tadyathā ḥ namo ratnatrayāya oṃ ālo tālo kālo sacchalo satvamudrati rakṣa rakṣa māṃ saparivārasya sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvabhayopadravebhyaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: Protect me from the fear of fire! Protect me from the fear of water! Protect me from the fear of serpents! Protect me from the fear of poison! Protect me from the fear of all adversaries and enemies! Protect me in tumultuous situations! Protect me in peaceful situations! Protect me when consciousness is lost! Protect me when consciousness is intact! Guard me from <s>nāgas</s>! Guard me from fierce beasts! Guard, guard me and all beings from all the wicked and corrupted ones! <s>Tadyathā</s>: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels)! Oṃ ālo tālo kālo sacchalo satvamudrati, guard, guard me together with my retinue and all beings from all fears and calamities, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.translated_text: Oṃ, O Deity <s>Mārīcī</s>, protect me on the road! Protect me on the wrong path! Protect me from the fear of men! Protect me from the fear of kings! Protect me from the fear of elephants! Protect me from the fear of thieves! Protect me from the fear of <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings)! Protect me from the fear of lions! Protect me from the fear of tigers! Protect me from the fear of horses!

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya / namo bhagavatyai āryamārīcīdevatāyai / tasyā hṛdayam āvartayiṣyāmi / tadyathā ḥ oṃ vattālī vadālī varālī varāhamukhī / sarvaduṣṭapraduṣṭānāṃ cakṣurmukhaṃ bandha bandha / bandha mukhaṃ jambhaya stambhaya mohaya svāhā / oṃ mārīcyai svāhā / oṃ varālī vadālī vattālī varāhamukhī sarvaduṣṭapraduṣṭānāṃ cakṣurmukhaṃ bandha bandha jambhaya jambhaya stambhaya stambhaya mohaya mohaya bhañjaya bhañjaya tarjaya tarjaya hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ* svāhā / oṃ mārīcyai sara sara muhya muhya vimuhya vimuhya apakrāmya apakrāmya sarvaduṣṭasatvān pathe utpathe sarvavidhnavināyakā apasarantu mā tiṣṭhantu triratnasatyena svāhā / oṃ caṇḍa paramacaṇḍa svāhā / oṃ agali pagali pañcagali sarvaduṣṭapraduṣṭānāṃ kāyavākcittaṃ mukhaṃ cakṣuṣi bandha bandha hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ* phaṭ* phaṭ* svāhā /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels)! Homage to the Blessed Noble Deity <s>Mārīcī</s>! I shall recite her <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra). <s>Tadyathā</s>: oṃ <s>Vattālī</s> <s>Vadālī</s> <s>Varālī</s> <s>Varāhamukhī</s> (Boar-faced One)! Bind, bind the eyes and faces of all the wicked and corrupted ones! Paralyze! Stupefy! <s>Svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to <s>Mārīcī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ <s>Varālī</s> <s>Vadālī</s> <s>Vattālī</s> <s>Varāhamukhī</s>! Bind, bind the eyes and faces of all the wicked and corrupted ones! Paralyze, paralyze! Stupefy, stupefy! Delude, delude! Shatter, shatter! Threaten, threaten! Hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ <s>Mārīcī</s>, flow, flow! Be deluded, be deluded! Be thoroughly deluded, be thoroughly deluded! Withdraw, withdraw! May all wicked beings on the road and off the road, and all obstacle-creating <s>Vināyakas</s>, depart and not remain—by the truth of the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ fierce one, supremely fierce one, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ agali pagali pañcagali, bind, bind the body, speech, mind, face, and eyes of all the wicked and corrupted ones! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanās te ca bhikṣavas te ca bodhisatvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragaruḍagandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti /
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). Those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and that entire assembly, and the world with its <s>devas</s> (gods), humans, <s>asuras</s> (demons), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), and <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians) rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
The <s>dhāraṇī</s> (protective spell) called Noble <s>Mārīcī</s> is complete.
